subject: Chemistry
question: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide is exactly neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of sulfuric acid: 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid.
response_text:
2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O

n(NaOH) = c × V = c × 0.0250 = 2.50 × 10⁻³ mol
n(H₂SO₄) = ½ × 2.50 × 10⁻³ = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol
[H₂SO₄] = 1.25 × 10⁻³ / 0.0200 = 0.0625 mol dm⁻³

The acid is diprotic, so it needs only half as many moles as the alkali.
